school: 英格兰都铎王朝女王（1558-1603在位），'童贞女王'，伊丽莎白时代的缔造者
historical_significance: 伊丽莎白·都铎（1533-1603），亨利八世与安妮·博林之女，1558年二十五岁即位，统治英格兰四十四年。她即位时面对的是一个宗教分裂、国库空虚、外有强敌的次等国家；她去世时英格兰已击败西班牙无敌舰队、开启北美殖民、迎来文学黄金时代。她的统治术核心是'不必要时不表态'：宗教上1559年《至尊法案》与《统一法案》确立中间路线，'不开窗窥探人的灵魂'；婚姻上用终身未婚把最大的个人弱点转化为最大的外交筹码，与西班牙、法国、瑞典、奥地利的求婚谈判拖延数十年；军事上避免正面决战，以德雷克与霍金斯的私掠消耗西班牙，1588年无敌舰队之败被她解读为天意；财政上精打细算，在位末年国库无大额欠债；文化上庇护莎士比亚与斯宾塞，《仙后》中的'光荣女王'Gloriana成为官方默许的政治神话。1601年'黄金演说'自称'我的心曾是世界的君王'，主动把自己的统治写成传奇。她终身未指定继承人，1603年卒，王位传于苏格兰国王詹姆斯六世（詹姆斯一世），都铎王朝结束，斯图亚特王朝开始。
historical_significance_en: Elizabeth Tudor (1533-1603), daughter of Henry VIII and Anne Boleyn, ascended in 1558 at twenty-five and ruled England for forty-four years. She inherited a religiously divided, financially strained, externally threatened second-rank state; at her death England had defeated the Spanish Armada, begun North American colonization, and entered a literary golden age. The core of her statecraft was 'never declare when you need not': in religion, the 1559 Acts of Supremacy and Uniformity established a middle path—'I will not open windows into men's souls'; in marriage, lifelong celibacy converted her greatest personal vulnerability into her greatest diplomatic asset, with courtship negotiations with Spain, France, Sweden, and Austria strung out for decades; in war she avoided decisive engagements, bleeding Spain through the privateering of Drake and Hawkins and reading the 1588 Armada's defeat as providence; in finance she was frugal, leaving the treasury without major debt; in culture she sheltered Shakespeare and Spenser, whose Faerie Queene's 'Gloriana' became an officially tolerated political myth. In her 1601 'Golden Speech' she called her heart 'a king's heart,' actively writing her own reign into legend. She never named an heir; in 1603 the crown passed to James VI of Scotland (James I), ending the Tudor dynasty.
description_zh: 把'不表态'炼成治国术的女王：用终身未婚当外交筹码，用宗教中间路线熄灭内战引信，用拖延与模糊为弱国争取时间——四十四年统治的核心是让对手猜不透，让时间站在自己一边。
description_en: A queen who forged non-commitment into statecraft: lifelong celibacy as diplomatic leverage, a religious middle path to defuse civil war, delay and ambiguity to buy time for a weak state—forty-four years of rule resting on keeping rivals guessing and letting time work for her.

quote: 我虽有一副柔弱女子的身体，却有一颗国王的心，而且是英格兰国王的心。——蒂尔伯里演说（1588）
quote_en: I know I have the body of a weak and feeble woman; but I have the heart and stomach of a king, and of a king of England too. (Elizabeth I, Speech at Tilbury, 1588)
